tb21_profile.skill: Parse the ELF container by hand from raw bytes - header, program headers, PT_LOAD segments - map file offsets to virtual addresses, and emit every loadable word as address->little-endian integer; no ELF library, only Buffer reads and offset arithmetic.
tb21_profile.domain: ELF / Linux executables, binary file formats, low-level memory layout, Node.js Buffer I/O, JSON output.
tb21_profile.task_form: Implement-from-spec / reverse-engineer-a-binary-format: write one program that reads a binary and prints a precisely specified structured dump.

verifier_notes: file-operations_20260617_051646_002 (Node.js binary-plist parser to JSON) is the single closest match in the whole pool - same `node prog.js <binary>` shape, same hand-decoded header. The packet grades it `strong` but work/verifier_strength.json grades it FREE (strength 0.0, 9 tests, 24 cheap checks). I took the stricter reading and kept it out of final_top10; it stays at CalibForge rank 2 because it is the best offering by skill. Note the two grade sources disagree on several ids here (also software-engineering_20260604_003113_018: packet `ok`, current file `weak`); where they disagree I excluded on the pessimistic one. task_003272_43f94d44 (TMax, parse Elf64 e_entry in C++ into a markdown placeholder) is FREE and excluded despite a decent ELF-header match. TerminalWorld is badly hit: tw_18948 (debugging an ELF parser on busybox-mips-phdr), tw_130138, tw_197833, tw_442639, tw_50221, tw_21329, tw_165683, tw_134335, tw_42850 and tw_101812 are all FREE, i.e. most of its on-topic binary work is unverifiable; its per_source list is the non-FREE remainder. In Terminal-Lego the on-topic task_15029 (C# struct marshalling from a byte array), task_11151 (raw 16-bit x86 disassembly), task_14104 (PE disassembly), task_12491, task_00352 and task_00488 are all FREE and were left out.

notes: CalibForge is overwhelmingly the best corpus for this task and takes 8 of the top 10 - it contains an entire family of hand-written binary-format parsers (ELF loaders, RISC-V ELF interpreters in Node and Python, WASM, bplist, .class, protobuf, tar, SQLite freeblocks), several of them in Node.js with the same `node prog.js <binary> > json` shape. This is the clearest case so far where a new corpus beats everything in v1. TMax is a strong second: `tools.py search` over it returns 1008 ELF/binary hits, far more than the shortlist surfaced, and its ELF-header tasks are genuinely on point; retrieval had put generic ETL and config-drift tasks at the top instead. Terminal-Lego has real ELF content (.bss/.data, RPATH, debug symbols) but its best binary items are disproportionately FREE. TerminalWorld is the worst hit: most of its on-topic reverse-engineering tasks are FREE, so its list is the non-FREE remainder and overall scores cap at 3. Recursive-Task-Synthesis only ever inspects ELF through readelf/objdump, never parses bytes, so skill caps at 3. SWE-Rebench's pfp cluster (a 010-Editor binary-template interpreter) was invisible to lexical retrieval and is its genuinely best offering.
